description.narrative: The training program of the DEA prepares entrepreneurs to export to the EU and enlarge their markets. The training consists of 5 days of training, coaching, and an assessment. All elements of the training have been highly valued by the participants and will be maintained. The DEA takes place twice a year, where companies need to have a minimum turnover and preferably focused on a specific sector (horticulture). The DEA allows the participants to dive into the specifics of their exporting and encourages peer-to-peer learning. It also allows the organizing team to organize workshops relevant to the selected sector, for example, sanitary requirements for fruits/vegetables during the DEA. Lastly, it is easier to create access to markets for specific products/services so this can also be facilitated better with the clustered edition.

title.narrative: Final Report on Dutch Export Academy

description.narrative: This report presents the findings and analysis of a comprehensive survey conducted to evaluate the effectiveness and impact of the 4th Edition of the Dutch Export Academy (DEA). The DEA's fourth edition comprised a 5-Day Academy training held in February and March 2023, along with a Study Visit to the Netherlands from April 16 to 22nd, 2023. The objective of the training program was to equip Ghanaian exporters and entrepreneurs with the necessary knowledge and skills to successfully navigate the complexities of the export market. By focusing on standards, business processes, and recognizing potential opportunities, participants were empowered to develop effective export strategies and optimize their export operations from Ghana to the European Union (EU) market. The Study Visit to the Netherlands had the purpose of giving participants useful information about effective EU export strategies, business practices, and cultural aspects that make international trade easier. This visit was meant to build on the training received in Ghana by providing participants with a direct experience of the Dutch export market. By talking to industry experts and learning about the cultural differences of doing business in the EU, participants gained a better understanding of how to apply the training they received. To assess the success and influence of the DEA 4th Edition, MDF West Africa conducted a thorough survey. The survey collected feedback from participants on the training program's significance, content, and its overall impact on their exporting abilities. This report aims to provide a comprehensive evaluation of the program's outcomes by analyzing the survey responses and identifying areas for improvement. The survey was carried out using an online tool, SurveyMonkey, after the DEA Training and Study Trip. Out of the 20 companies that participated, 15 responded to the survey. Furthermore, recommendations are provided to enhance the program's effectiveness and address any identified limitations, ensuring its continuous improvement in future editions.

title.narrative: Year End Report of DEA 5th Edition

description.narrative: The primary objective of the DEA program is to prepare Ghanaian exporters and entrepreneurs to navigate the complexities of the export market successfully. This report evaluates the fifth edition of the program, highlighting its activities, outcomes, and areas for improvement. The fifth edition of the DEA comprised three main components:  A 9-day training program in May 2024 covered key areas such as export finance, export processes, and the business model canvas.  A 3-day intermission program in June 2024 provided practical guidance on developing export plans, contracting, negotiation, and one-on-one coaching.  A 5-day Export Study Visit to the Netherlands in September 2024, where participants engaged with key industry players, explored market opportunities, and gained insights into cultural nuances essential for international trade.
